canonical_name: WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy) benchmark; subsets WMDP-Bio / WMDP-Chem / WMDP-Cyber
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03218 (v1 submitted 5 Mar 2024 18:59 UTC; dataset+code public same day: https://github.com/centerforaisafety/wmdp initial commit 2024-03-05)
metric: accuracy (% correct, 4-option multiple choice), reported per subset (Bio/Chem/Cyber); no single leaderboard aggregate; WMDP-Bio treated as headline subset (most reported by labs)
direction: higher (capability reading = more hazardous knowledge; in the unlearning use-case lower is better; random=25%)
human_baseline: none published by creators (paper: no human/expert performance given)
ab_system: Grok 4.20 single-agent ('Grok 4.2 SA' in card), xAI, pre-mitigation
ab_mode: accuracy, pass@1 (card does not state tool use or shots)
score_at_release: GPT-4: WMDP-Bio 81.6, WMDP-Cyber 51.8, WMDP-Chem 59.7 (paper v1 Table 2, v1 dataset of 4,157 Qs)
n_items: 3668 (current release: Bio+Chem+Cyber; v1 had 4157 = Bio 1520 / Cyber 2225 / Chem 412; trimmed 2024-04-23)
lineage: no parent; RMU/unlearning companion method; dataset revised 2024-03-08 (Cyber choice randomization) and 2024-04-23 (items removed/reformatted; paper v3). No successor found.
best_by_cutoff: WMDP-Bio 91 / WMDP-Cyber 91 / WMDP-Chem 90: Grok 4.20 SA (xAI), model card 2026-04-07; later xAI cards lower (Grok 4.5 high Bio 90.9/Chem 87.3 2026-07-16; Grok 4.6 high 90.0/85.3/Cyber 90.1 2026-08-12; Grok 4.7 high 88.1/84.9/88.1 2026-09-21); Meta Muse Spark 1.1 Bio 89.0 (2026-07-09)
notes: (1) Tool-assisted result NOT counted: OpenAI deep research system card (https://cdn.openai.com/deep-research-system-card.pdf, dated 2025-02-25; lab_reports lists 2025-02-02 = product launch) reports 'WMDP Biology: Pre and Post-Mitigation deep research with browsing score 90%, while o1 and o3-mini score 86%'; card says browsing adds ~3 pts and that the published benchmark is considered contaminated => no-browsing ~87%. WMDP standard protocol is closed-book MCQ, so tool result excluded; if one counted it, AB would be 2025-02 (OpenAI, scaffold, self). (2) OpenAI used a 1,520-question bio subset (= v1 Bio size), not the current trimmed set. (3) Lab line date 2026-02-17 for Grok 4.20 is the beta release; the score was publicly disclosed in the card dated 2026-04-07 (xAI card URL date), so ab_date=2026-04. (4) xAI Table 4 also lists a 'human baseline' of 0.61 (Bio) / 0.43 (Chem) - xAI's own label, not from WMDP creators, and <85% anyway => criterion B. (5) Subset choice does not change the date: same xAI card has Bio 0.91, Cyber 0.91, Chem 0.90; weighted mean ~0.91. (6) Gemini 2.5 report shows WMDP Bio/Chem only in Figure 9 (no numbers in text); o1 system card (2024-09-12) says only that WMDP bio/chem 'contextual evaluations' were run, no scores; Gemini 3 Pro FSF report has no WMDP mention; Meta Muse Spark WMDP-Cyber 89.8 (2026-04-08) and Bio 89.0 (2026-07-09) are below 90. (7) Strict event not found: no organizer-verified or independent run >=90 located (inspect_evals README has no results table). No C/D/E: README at 2025-05-29 shows no deprecation; OpenAI's 'contaminated' remark is a lab caveat, not independent evidence. (8) Sources: arXiv API (export.arxiv.org) blocked in this environment; arxiv.org/a/ author page rate-limited (HTTP 429); numbers read via WebFetch summaries of PDFs (small-model summarizer).

ab_system: DeBERTaV3-large + KEAR (Microsoft Cognitive Services Research; single fine-tuned model with retrieved external knowledge text: ConceptNet, dictionary, training-data retrieval)
ab_mode: single-model accuracy on dev (fine-tuned; external-attention knowledge retrieval); same paper: ensemble of 39 models 93.4 dev
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.03254v1 (Table 4; arXiv id 2112.03254 => v1 Dec 2021); 91.2 re-confirmed as 'DeBERTaV3-large+KEAR (Xu et al., 2022)' prior-SOTA in PaLM 2 report Table 5 footnote e (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.10403v1)
score_at_release: 55.9 (BERT-large on the random split; paper text: 'about 56%', well below the human 88.9)
n_items: 12102 (v1.11 per tau-nlp.org; train 9,741 [KEAR Table 6], validation 1,221 [inspect_evals README], test = 1,140 derived by subtraction, labels hidden); original paper: 12,247
lineage: CSQA v1.0 (3-choice leaderboard, discontinued per tau-nlp.org) -> v1.11 (5-choice, 12,102 Qs, current). Same-group successor CommonsenseQA 2.0 (arXiv 2201.05320, Jan 2022; yes/no, gamified) - its text does not call CSQA saturated, so no C-via-successor.
best_by_cutoff: Dev: 93.4 (KEAR ensemble of 39, Dec 2021; single 91.2). Hidden test (leaderboard): 89.4 (KEAR ensemble, ~Dec 2021; single 86.1). LLM self-reports: PaLM 2-L 90.4 (7-shot CoT+SC, 2023-05-10); Llama 3.1 405B 85.8 (2024-07-23). No higher result located by 2026-09-30 (leaderboard unreachable).
notes: Hardest calls: (1) Criterion A vs B: human 88.9 is a majority vote of 5 crowd workers on 100 random questions (split unspecified) => aggregate => B (threshold 90). If A (88.9) were used the date is the same month: KEAR 89.4 (ensemble of 39, hidden test leaderboard) and 91.2/93.4 dev, all Dec 2021 (arXiv 2112.03254; paper title 'Human Parity on CommonsenseQA'). (2) split=dev: test labels hidden (inspect_evals README: 'test split's labels are not public'; KEAR reports 'official leaderboard result on the hidden test set'); community (LLM papers, lm-eval) reports dev, so dev counted per rule 6a. On hidden test no >=90 result found (best 89.4 ensemble), so the event rests on dev. (3) Strict event left empty: needs official-test or organizer-verified single model >=90; none found. PaLM 2-L 90.4 (2023-05-10) is a self-report with CoT+self-consistency (dev, split not stated). (4) First-by-time: nothing >=90 on dev found before KEAR; KEAR prior results in its table: UnifiedQA 79.1, ALBERT+KD 80.3, DEKCOR ~80.7-83.3 (test). Possible earlier leaderboard-entry date for KEAR (before arXiv) could not be checked (AI2 leaderboard, tau-nlp leaderboard table, paperswithcode unreachable/robots-blocked); arXiv v1 date taken from the arXiv id (2112.xxxxx = Dec 2021; abs page metadata not returned by fetch tool). (5) No C (tau-nlp page: only v1.0 3-choice leaderboard 'discontinued'; v1.11 active; CSQA2 does not name saturation), no D, no E found. Not abandoned: event occurred. Last lab report 2024-07-23 (Meta Llama 3.1). (6) Lab-report scores for PaLM/Mistral blank in input; PaLM 2 7-shot CoT 90.4 read from Table 5 of the PaLM 2 report via summarizer.

canonical_name: AA-Omniscience (Artificial Analysis Omniscience Index; public subset AA-Omniscience-Public)
release_source: https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/aa-omniscience-knowledge-hallucination-benchmark (article dated November 16, 2025); arXiv v1 17 Nov 2025 https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13029
metric: Omniscience Index OI = 100*(correct - incorrect)/(all questions), abstain = 0, bounded -100..100 (also reports Accuracy % and Hallucination Rate %)
direction: higher (Index and Accuracy; Hallucination Rate is lower-better but not the headline metric)
threshold: 90 (on Omniscience Index; scale max 100; same 90 if Accuracy% used)
score_at_release: Omniscience Index 4.8 (highest; only three models above 0)
n_items: 6000 (42 topics, 6 domains); public subset ~10% (~600) on HF as ArtificialAnalysis/AA-Omniscience-Public; remaining ~90% private
lineage: No parent. Public subset AA-Omniscience-Public (~600 Qs). No version change or deprecation notice found on the AA evaluation page (read 2026-10-03).
best_by_cutoff: Omniscience Index 46 = Claude Opus 5.5 (AA leaderboard page read 2026-10-03; entry date not shown, model released 2026-09-22); GPT-6 Astra (High) 44; Claude Fable 5.1 43; top Accuracy 67% = Claude Fable 5.1 (same page). Far below 90.
notes: Hardest call = stratum. Coded main because headline metric is factual recall with a calibration-aware score on a bounded scale, with public paper, public subset and public leaderboard. Borderline propensity: Index rewards abstention/penalizes hallucination, Anthropic system cards file it under 'Honesty > Factual questions' (Opus 4.5 card section 4.1). If the study treats hallucination/honesty metrics as propensity, this unit would be 'propensity' (identification fields only). Scale/threshold: Index range is -100..100 (max 100) so B threshold = 90; accuracy 0-100 gives the same 90. No unit is near it (best Index 46, best accuracy 67), so no AB/strict event; no C/D/E found; not abandoned (Anthropic reports it through 2026-09-28). Lab-report scores are blank in the input (cards show charts/relative gains only; e.g., Opus 4.5 card gives only '8.2% improvement with 16k thinking' in text). Sonnet 5 card line says 'public split; net score'. Questions generated by an automated question-generation agent from academic/industry sources, then filtered/revised (paper) => curation synthetic. best_by_cutoff date is not shown on the AA page; Opus 5.5 system card is dated 2026-09-22, so the 46 was most likely posted by the cutoff but this is not documented. The '36% accuracy' for Claude 4.1 Opus in a summarizer pass was not re-verified and is not used. Fetched via WebFetch (small-model summaries); export.arxiv.org and huggingface.co unreachable.

canonical_name: ASDiv (Academia Sinica Diverse MWP Dataset), full set; arithmetic subset ASDiv-A treated as separate unit

metric: answer (solution) accuracy; original protocol 5-fold cross-validation, LLM papers score the whole set (2,096-2,215 numeric-answer problems)
human_baseline: none reported by creators (paper only says SOTA systems 'not competitive with human performance')
ab_system: GPT-4 (OpenAI), CoT prompting, as tabulated by ToRA authors (Gou et al.); same table: GPT-4 (PAL) 92.6, ChatGPT 87.3
ab_mode: few-shot CoT, single answer (pass@1); full ASDiv test set 2,215 samples in ToRA
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.17452 (ToRA, Table 2; arXiv id 2309.17452 = Sep 2023, repo initial commit 2023-09-27)
strict_system: GPT-4 (CoT), third-party table in ToRA (single model, no verifier)
strict_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.17452 (Table 2); provenance (own run vs cited) not stated in the paper text
score_at_release: UnitDep 0.37, GTS 0.36, LCA++ 0.36 on ASDiv (5-fold CV); GTS 0.68 on ASDiv-A; paper: 'overall performance is only around 36% on ASDiv'
n_items: 2305 problems (ASDiv); ASDiv-A 1,218; LLM papers use 2,096 (DiVeRSe, RE2) or 2,215 (ToRA) numeric-answer variants
lineage: No parent. Official arithmetic subset ASDiv-A (1,218 MWPs, own named subset => separate unit; results on it only noted here). No successor by the same authors found.
best_by_cutoff: GPT-4 (PAL) 92.6, GPT-4 CoT 91.3 (ToRA Table 2, 2023-09). Later higher scores likely exist but were not systematically searched; no lab-report line is >=90 (DeepSeek-Coder PAL 76.7; Llama 2-Chat tool use 67.1).
notes: Search backwards found nothing >=90 before ToRA: PoT (Nov 2022) 85.2 (Codex; PaL 79.6), DiVeRSe (Jun 2022) 88.7 with code-davinci-002 (self-consistency 86.2; PaLM-540B SC 81.9; prior fine-tuned SOTA 75.3), Re-Reading paper (Sep 2023) ChatGPT 85.6-88.4. First >=90 = GPT-4 in ToRA Table 2 (Sep 2023); the ToRA text does not say whether its GPT-4 numbers were run by the authors or cited, so an earlier source may exist (kept date_upper_bound=0 but confidence medium). arXiv date stamp of ToRA could not be read via fetch; month taken from arXiv id 2309 and GitHub initial commit 2023-09-27. ASDiv-A (arithmetic subset) results by symbolic/fine-tuned solvers are a separate unit per codebook 1.6 and were not used. Tools: ASDiv has no tool-free standard protocol (original solvers output equations), so program-aided results would count; the CoT (no-tool) 91.3 already qualifies. Strict event: no official test split exists (5-fold CV); I treated third-party single-model run as the strict qualifier. No C (repo README last changed 2022-12-07 for license text only), no D/E found. Not abandoned (event occurred). Lab reports 2022-2023 only (Google PaLM, Meta Llama 2, DeepSeek-Coder). Sources read via WebFetch summaries; export.arxiv.org blocked; paperswithcode unreachable.

lineage: Rolling; versions livebench-2024-06-24, 07-26, 08-31, 11-25, 2025-04-02, 04-25, 05-30 (agentic coding added), 10-03 (agent switched to Mini-SWE-Agent), 11-25, 12-23, 2026-01-08 (changelog). Coding questions drawn from LiveCodeBench until 2025-04-25; reasoning web_of_lies partly from BIG-Bench Extra Hard since 2025-04-02. Scores are not comparable across versions.

Lab-reported (version livebench-2024-11-25): Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 78.4 (2025-07-25), Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 75.4, Kimi K2 76.4, QwQ-32B 73.1; category scores can be higher (o3-mini high Coding 84.6, secondary source). These are routine refreshes of a rolling benchmark, not withdrawal/replacement; repo still active (commits through 2026-09-29, e.g., Grok 4.7 and gpt-6.x configs). No E evidence found. Not abandoned: leaderboard active; last lab-report line in input is 2025-10-30 (<12 months before cutoff). Unit mixes sub-names ('LiveBench (Coding)' category scores from OpenAI o1/o3-mini lines are category scores, not the global average). Leaderboard history/current scores unreachable (livebench.ai is JS-only; huggingface.co blocked), so best_by_cutoff is from lab lines only. Sources read: GitHub changelog/README, arXiv abs.

canonical_name: XWinograd (XWINO / X-WINOGRAD; Tikhonov & Ryabinin 2021, extended by Muennighoff et al. 2022 with Chinese 16->504)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12066 (Findings of ACL 2021; arXiv id 2106 = June 2021); dataset repo https://github.com/yandex-research/crosslingual_winograd initial commit 2021-06-24
metric: accuracy on 2-way pronoun-resolution (Winograd schema), reported per language (en, fr, ja/jp, pt, ru, zh); dataset-level = mean over languages
human_baseline: none reported by creators (paper: no human performance baseline)
abandoned_evidence: Only lab reporting it is Alibaba/Qwen (Qwen1.5 2024-02-04 ... Qwen2.5 tech report 2024-12-19, always inside the aggregate 'Understanding' score with BELEBELE/XCOPA/XStoryCloze/PAWS-X, never a separate number); input lists no lab report after 2024-12-19 (21 months before cutoff). No leaderboard exists for XWinograd, so there is no leaderboard activity to observe; third-party use after 2024 was not verifiable with the allowed tools.
score_at_release: XLM-R-Large attention-head method (creators' best): en 66.7, fr 67.5, ja 69.1, ru 70.4, zh 60.0, pt 66.8 (paper Table 3; chance 50)
n_items: 4449 in current HF/Muennighoff version (en 2,325; fr 83; jp 959; pt 263; ru 315; zh 504); original 2021 release 3,961 (zh 16)
lineage: Compiles existing Winograd-schema sets (WSC273, SuperGLUE WSC, DPR; French WSC, Japanese WSC translation, Russian RWSD, Chinese WSC, Portuguese WSC). Original name XWINO/X-WINOGRAD (2021-06). Extended to Chinese 504 items and renamed XWinograd in Muennighoff et al., 'Crosslingual Generalization through Multitask Finetuning' (arXiv 2211.01786, Nov 2022; ACL 2023) - the version Qwen cites.
best_by_cutoff: 6-language mean accuracy: Aya-23-35B 84.4, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct 83.1 (0-shot; Aya 23 paper arXiv 2405.15032, 2024-05). Qwen2/2.5 numbers exist only inside an aggregate 'Understanding' average. No per-language or mean value >=90 found; per-language English numbers for frontier models not retrievable.
notes: Hardest calls: (1) Which metric/subset is primary: no leaderboard and no official aggregate; I used the mean over six languages (as in Aya 23 / xP3) and B threshold 90. If the English subset alone (2,325 items from WSC273/SuperGLUE WSC/DPR) were primary, a >=90 result by strong 2023-2025 LLMs is plausible (e.g., PaLM 2-L Winograd 89.5 1-shot and WSC 86.9 are on the original sets, not XWinograd) but I could not find any documented per-language >=90 figure, so no AB event is coded; a coder with access to lm-eval/Swallow/other per-language tables might date a saturation event. (2) Status: coded 'abandoned' because the only lab reporter (Qwen) stopped after 2024-12-19 and there is no leaderboard; this is the literal reading of the abandonment rule and could instead be 'alive' if third-party usage is counted. (3) Birth: 2021-06 (first public corpus); the named 'XWinograd' extended release is Nov 2022 (xP3 paper, arXiv 2211.01786 id-derived date). (4) Qwen lab lines have blank scores because Qwen reports XWinograd only as a component of the multilingual 'Understanding' average (checked Qwen2 report 2407.10671 and Qwen2.5 report 2412.15115: no per-dataset numbers). PaLM 2 report has no XWinograd. (5) No C/D/E found. Tools: WebFetch summaries of PDFs; export.arxiv.org and huggingface.co (dataset card, leaderboards) unreachable.

canonical_name: SimpleQA (OpenAI; Wei et al., 'Measuring short-form factuality in large language models')
release_source: https://openai.com/index/introducing-simpleqa/ (post dated October 30, 2024; github.com/openai/simple-evals 'add simpleqa' commit 2024-10-29/30); arXiv v1 7 Nov 2024 https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04368
metric: 'Correct' accuracy (% of all questions answered correctly) as graded by an LLM autorater into correct / incorrect / not attempted; F-score (harmonic mean of correct and correct-given-attempted) also reported
human_baseline: none presented as human performance; paper's data-quality check: a third AI trainer answered a random 1,000-question sample with 94.4% agreement with reference answers, inherent label error ~3%
score_at_release: o1-preview 42.7% correct (F-score 44.8); GPT-4o 38.2; Claude-3.5-sonnet 28.9; o1-mini 8.1 (paper main table)
lineage: No parent. Cleaned 1,000-prompt derivative SimpleQA Verified (Google DeepMind, different authors; arXiv 2509.07968 v1 2025-09-09) is a separate unit. Chinese SimpleQA (C-SimpleQA / CSimpleQA lines in the input) is a different benchmark and was excluded from this unit.
best_by_cutoff: No-tools (standard protocol): GPT-4.5 62.5% correct (OpenAI, 2025-02-27, also reproduced in simple-evals README); GPT-5 55% (no browsing, 2025-08-07); Gemini 2.5 Pro 54.0% (2025-06). Tool-assisted, NOT counted: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp agentic tool use 97.1 (2025-09-29), V3.1-Terminus 96.8 (2025-09-22), Grok 4 Fast with search 95.0% (2025-09-19), Perplexity Deep Research 93.9% (2025-02-14), DeepSeek-V3.1 search agent 93.4 (2025-08-21), ChatGPT agent 91.4 (2025-07-17). Gemini 3 Pro 72.1% is on SimpleQA Verified (different unit).
notes: Hardest call = tools. SimpleQA is a closed-book (parametric knowledge) test: OpenAI's reference grader treats 'Without researching the web, I cannot answer this question' as NOT_ATTEMPTED (simple-evals/simpleqa_eval.py), GPT-5 system card labels its line 'SimpleQA [no browsing]', and the benchmark is framed around whether models 'know what they know'. I therefore did not count search/browsing/agent results for the main event; all lab-reported no-tools results in the input are far below 90 (best 62.5). If tool-assisted results were counted, AB would be 2025-02 (Perplexity Deep Research 93.9% accuracy, self-report, agent/scaffold; https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/introducing-perplexity-deep-research dated Feb 14, 2025) - that reading would make status 'saturated' (B, 2025-02). I did not search for earlier tool-assisted claims. Human baseline: the 94.4% third-trainer agreement is a quality check, not presented as human performance, so criterion B (A would give threshold 94.4; ceiling is also limited by ~3% label noise). No C: simple-evals README (deprecation notice 2025-07-09) only stops updating its results table and says the repo 'will continue to host reference implementations for ... SimpleQA'; SimpleQA Verified is by different authors (Google DeepMind), so no C-via-successor. No E: SimpleQA Verified paper lists problematic labels/biases/redundancy but quantifies no >=20% defective-item audit (funnel removals are mostly dedup/topic balancing; source reconciliation removes ~3-4%), and no lab statement of stopping because of it was verified. Not abandoned: last lab line in input is 2025-10-30 (<12 months before cutoff). No newer no-tools SimpleQA numbers located (labs appear to have moved to SimpleQA Verified; Kaggle leaderboard not readable). Input lines 'C-SimpleQA'/'CSimpleQA' (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen) excluded; 'SimpleQA Hallucination Rate' is not the primary metric. Sources via WebFetch summaries.

canonical_name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH; 23 tasks / 27 subtasks from BIG-bench)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.09261 (v1 Mon 17 Oct 2022); data repo https://github.com/suzgunmirac/BIG-Bench-Hard initial commit 2022-10-15, data commit 2022-10-17
metric: exact-match accuracy averaged over the 23 tasks (3-shot CoT is the common protocol; answer-only also reported in paper)
human_baseline: 67.7 (average human-rater over 23 tasks; max human-rater 94.4; random 25.7; best prior BIG-bench model 52.1) - paper Table 2
human_type: average human (raters enlisted by BIG-bench organizers; 'not fully representative of the entire population')
ab_mode: 3-shot CoT, single model, exact match average
ab_source: https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/fed9cc193a14b84131812372d8d5857f8f304c52/Model_Card_Claude_3_Addendum.pdf (Table 1: 'BIG-Bench Hard ... 3-shot CoT | 93.1% | 86.8% ...'); announcement https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-5-sonnet dated Jun 21, 2024 (lab line says 2024-06-20)
score_at_release: Codex (code-davinci-002) CoT 73.9 (answer-only 56.6); InstructGPT CoT 68.4; PaLM 540B CoT 65.2 (AO 52.3); avg human-rater 67.7
lineage: Subset of BIG-bench (Srivastava et al., arXiv 2206.04615, Jun 2022): the 23 tasks on which prior models did not beat the average human-rater. Successor BIG-Bench Extra Hard (BBEH, Google DeepMind, arXiv 2502.19187 v1 2025-02-26) replaces each BBH task with a harder one.
best_by_cutoff: 93.2 Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new), 3-shot CoT, Anthropic model card 2024-10-22; 93.1 Claude 3.5 Sonnet 2024-06; base models: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-Base 90.98 (2026-02-16), Qwen2.5-Max base 89.3 (2025-01-28), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash base 86.1 (2026-09-10). No later higher figure in lab lines.
notes: Criterion: creators' 'human performance' = average human-rater 67.7 (<85) so B; max human-rater 94.4 is not used per the average-of-type rule. AB: first >=90 in lab lines is Claude 3.5 Sonnet 93.1 (2024-06); earlier lab results are all below 90 (Flan-PaLM BBH-nlp 78.4 2022-10; PaLM 2-L 78.1; Gemini Ultra 83.6 2023-12; Claude 3 Opus 86.8 2024-03; Gemini 1.5 Pro 89.2 2024-05, just below). I could not search exhaustively for earlier scaffold/ensemble results, hence medium confidence. The Anthropic PDF has no explicit date; month taken from the announcement (Jun 21, 2024) and input line (2024-06-20). Strict event not found: no organizer-verified or independent single-model run >=90 located (BBH has no leaderboard; the 93.1 is a self-report). C not coded: BBEH (Kazemi et al., Google DeepMind, 2025-02-26, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.19187) says 'The original BIG-Bench dataset became saturated ... state-of-the-art models achieve near-perfect scores on many tasks in BBH, thus diminishing its utility' and replaces BBH, but only 2 of 20 BBEH authors (Yi Tay, Quoc V. Le) overlap with the 11 BBH authors and the BBH repo owner/lead authors are absent, so I judged it not 'substantial author overlap' under rule 6a. If the study counts it as C the date would be 2025-02 (later than AB, so primary_date unchanged). No D/E found. Not abandoned.
